reason: Conversation 1 gave the key safety instruction explicitly ('stop using it, leave it unplugged, don't keep wiggling it') once the taped cable and flicker emerged, and routed the fix to the handy son or a repair shop with sensible, correctly priced options (shorten-and-replug or full cable swap) without asking the elderly customer to open anything. Its one weakness is over-certainty ('That's your answer... almost certainly') when a blown fuse or switch can't be excluded remotely, plus an early speculative mention of carbon brushes. Conversation 2 was more concise but never clearly told her to stop using it, missed the opportunity to involve the son she mentioned, and gave inaccurate advice that a Henry cable fix 'usually requires soldering and heat-shrink tubing' while suggesting a replacement unit for what is a cheap cable repair.
